primer.mentalModel: Think of character classes as engine shortcuts. Instead of manually writing ranges like [0-9] or [a-zA-Z0-9_], these single-letter tokens instantly tell the regex engine to match digits, word characters, or spacing.
points: \w matches any single word character: letters (a-z, A-Z), numbers (0-9), and underscores (_).
\s matches any single whitespace character (spaces, tabs, and line breaks).
Inversion Rule: Capitalizing the token inverts its meaning—\D (non-digit), \W (non-word), \S (non-whitespace).
pitfalls: \w does NOT match punctuation or special symbols (like @, #, $, or hyphens -). A string like 'user-name' contains two \w blocks separated by a \W hyphen.
\d, \w, and \s match exactly ONE character at a time unless combined with a quantifier like + or *.
\s includes hidden characters like tabs (\t) and line breaks (\n), not just standard keyboard spaces.

examples.note: Matches sequence of letters, numbers, and underscores
Inverted class matches everything that is NOT a digit

positive.hint: Use \w+ to match letters, numbers, and underscores
